A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, eight tables, six figures, and Appendices A.1–A.5 support comparison despite reformatting and figure relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic benchmark evaluations, real-data reconstruction results, ablations, and camera-parameter robustness experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the synthetic and real-data comparisons and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The optimal-transport loss, Sinkhorn implementation, iterative encoder-decoder architecture, differentiable image reconstruction, and inference thresholding remain unchanged. Revised method paragraphs describe the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same EPFL synthetic density/SNR regimes, Tubulin, NPC-Nup107, NPC-Nup96, temporally binned scenarios, and camera-mismatch test data. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains 3D-DAOSTORM, DECODE, and LiteLoc; Table 2 retains LiteLoc; Figure 4 retains 3D-DAOSTORM and LiteLoc. The decoder and Hungarian-versus-Sinkhorn comparisons also retain their original alternatives.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, matching tolerances, evaluation metrics, threshold optimization, temporal binning, and camera-jitter procedures are unchanged. Condensed descriptions in Section 4 do not revise the experimental settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablation, decoder comparison, coordinate-range sensitivity, transport-solver comparison, and camera-mismatch analysis. The coordinate-range study moves from Figure 6 in v1 to Figure 5 in v2 without changing its evidence.

E5.justification: The four training seeds in Table 1, three seeds in Tables 5 and 7, and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. The new reproducibility statement mentions repository seed settings but provides no additional seed values, run counts, or statistical analyses.

E6.justification: All entries and numerical values in Tables 1–8 are unchanged, as are the plotted sensitivity results and qualitative reconstructions. For example, Table 1 retains E3D = 0.750 ± 0.004 for the proposed method at density 2.0 and high SNR.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), the mathematical formulations, noise assumptions, and differentiable reconstruction derivation are retained. Shortened explanations introduce no new definitions, assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: optimal-transport training without NMS, physics-informed iterative refinement, and improved localization at moderate/high densities. Copyediting does not change these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of the ablations and robustness results, temporal-binning caveat, computational limitations, and PSF-calibration dependence remain unchanged. The new ethics statement adds general societal assurances rather than scientific limitations or mechanisms.

D1.justification: v1 provides a repository link and implementation details. v2 adds a Reproducibility Statement specifying that the same repository supplies source code, training/evaluation scripts, configured hyperparameters and seeds, and Python environment specifications. This expands documentation without establishing that the resources themselves changed.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the positioning relative to SMLM methods, optimal-transport set matching, and iterative refinement remains substantively unchanged. Related-work paragraphs are shortened without introducing new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar and spelling, condenses selected related-work and technical explanations, updates affiliations and acknowledgements, and adds ethics and reproducibility statements. The main section sequence and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The document adopts the ICLR layout throughout, with a redesigned title/author block, narrower text area, rescaled tables, and relocated figures and algorithm display. Appendix Figures 5 and 6 exchange numbering and positions; their underlying content is retained.

improvement.justification: Copyediting and condensed explanations modestly improve clarity, while the new Reproducibility Statement makes the documented reproduction resources more explicit. The scientific evidence is unchanged. The narrower layout makes Table 1 smaller, a readability tradeoff that limits the overall gain.
